## ip_locations: Where the IP addresses in the records are registered
IP address 203.0.113.24 — according to Example IP Database, 2025-10-01: registered to Example Hosting Network (AS64500), location Example City, Exampleland (accuracy about 50 km). (E4)
The database lists this network as a hosting or VPN provider. (E4)
IP address 198.51.100.7 — according to Example IP Database, 2025-10-01: registered to Example Mobile Network (AS64501), location Example Town, Exampleland (accuracy about 100 km). (E4)
IP address 192.0.2.150 — according to Example IP Database, 2025-10-01: registered to Example VPN Service (AS64502). (E4)
The database lists this network as a hosting or VPN provider. (E4)
The institution's record gives the location as Exampleland. (E4)
An IP location is the provider's estimate of where the network is registered or used. It can differ from where the person was, for example on mobile data, a VPN or a hosting service. Addresses can be reassigned over time; this lookup used a database dated 2025-10-01.
## account_access_sequence: The sequence the records show

- 3. The complainant states that this device is not theirs.

- 5. The record shows a payee added at 21:20 on 3 July 2025 from this device, authorised by digital token. (E4)
- 9. The complainant reported to the institution on 4 July 2025. The record shows access to the account blocked at 09:30 on 4 July 2025. (E4)

## customer_conduct_comparison: The conduct the records show, and what each document refers to
The complainant states that they entered their credentials, card details or a one-time code on a fake website or app.
The E-Payments User Protection Guidelines do not refer to entering credentials, card details or a code on a website or app.
The record shows 3 alerts, the first sent at 21:06 on 3 July 2025 to registered mobile number. The complainant reported to the institution on 4 July 2025, 1 calendar day after the first alert. (E4)
The E-Payments User Protection Guidelines refer to notifications and alerts from the institution in footnote 20 (R5).
The record shows access blocked at 09:30 on 4 July 2025, channel recorded as 'hotline'. (E4)
The E-Payments User Protection Guidelines do not refer to blocking access.
The complainant reported to the police on 4 July 2025. (E3)
The E-Payments User Protection Guidelines do not refer to reporting to the police.
The Shared Responsibility Framework Guidelines have no test of the account user's conduct.
The institution's letter describes the complainant's conduct as 'negligent'. The conduct it cites is entered the account password and a one-time code on a website reached from a message. (E2)
The E-Payments User Protection Guidelines use the term 'recklessness'.
The institution's own terms in force on 3 July 2025 are not held for that date.
